Join 𝑃 to 𝑂 to 𝑄. 
The angle at the centre ( |∠𝑃𝑂𝑄| ) must be twice 
|∠𝑃𝑅𝑄|, so must be > 180°. 
So, the point 𝑂 has to be outside the triangle 𝑃𝑄𝑅. 
OR 
Assume that 𝑂 is inside the triangle 𝑃𝑄𝑅. 
Then |∠𝑃𝑂𝑄| < 180°, 
where ∠𝑃𝑂𝑄 is the angle in the triangle 𝑃𝑂𝑄. 
But |∠𝑃𝑅𝑄| is half this angle, so |∠𝑃𝑅𝑄| < 90°, 
a contradiction. 
OR 
Assume that 𝑂 is inside the triangle 𝑃𝑄𝑅. 
Join 𝑃 to 𝑂 and continue until you hit the circle 𝑘, 
on the minor arc between 𝑅 and 𝑄. Label this 
point 𝑆. 
Then |∠𝑃𝑅𝑆| = 90°, as [𝑃𝑆] is a diameter. 
But |𝑃𝑅𝑆| > |∠𝑃𝑅𝑄|, a contradiction. 
OR 
The line through 𝑅 perpendicular to 𝑃𝑅 intersects 
𝑘 on the arc joining 𝑃 to 𝑄 that doesn’t contain 𝑅. 
Label this point 𝑇. Join 𝑇 to 𝑃. The centre is the 
midpoint of [𝑇𝑃], which is outside the triangle 
𝑃𝑄𝑅.
